passages.heading: <acronym> HTML acronym or abbreviation element
passages.text: Avoid using this feature in new projects. This feature may be a candidate for removal from web standards or browsers. See full compatibility Learn more The <acronym> HTML element allows authors to clearly indicate a sequence of characters that compose an acronym or abbreviation for a word. Warning: Don't use this element. Use the <abbr> element instead.

passages.heading: Attributes
passages.text: This element only has global attributes, which are common to all elements.

passages.heading: DOM Interface
passages.text: This element implements the HTMLElement interface.

passages.heading: Examples
passages.text: The WWW is only a component of the Internet.

passages.heading: Default styling
passages.text: Though the purpose of this tag is purely for the convenience of the author, its default styling varies from one browser to another: Opera, Firefox, Chrome, and some others add a dotted underline to the content of the element. A few browsers not only add a dotted underline, but also put it in small caps; to avoid this styling, adding something like font-variant: none in the CSS takes care of this case. It is therefore recommended that web authors either explicitly style this element, or accept some cross-browser variation.
